extracted.intended_audience: employers petitioning for R-1 religious worker status, immigration practitioners, and law enforcement agencies filing S-classification requests
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements, evidentiary standards, procedures, and discretionary rules for filing and adjudicating R-1 religious worker petitions, NATO dependent employment, and S nonimmigrant (witness/informant) classification requests under 8 CFR. Includes attestation, documentation, inspection, revocation, and interagency certification procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on total stay for R-1 aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who has spent five years in the United States in R-1 status may not receive an extension of stay in the United States as an R-1 nonimmigrant and must depart after reaching the five-year maximum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No minimum outside-the-U.S. period required before seeking readmission as R-1, provided other eligibility requirements are met. Exceptions: (1) aliens who did not reside continually because employment was seasonal or intermittent or was for an aggregate of six months or less per year; and (2) aliens who reside abroad and regularly commute to the U.S. to engage in part-time employment. Both petitioner and alien must provide clear and convincing proof for exceptions (e.g., arrival/departure records, tax return transcripts, employment records).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and filing procedures for R-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An employer in the United States seeking to employ a religious worker shall file a petition in accordance with the applicable form instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific USCIS form instructions for jurisdiction, required supplements, and filing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer attestation requirements for R-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorized official of the prospective employer must complete, sign, date, and submit a USCIS-prescribed attestation with the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The attestation must specifically confirm: (i) the petitioner is a bona fide non-profit religious organization or bona fide affiliated organization exempt from taxation; (ii) the alien has been a member of the denomination for at least two years and is otherwise qualified; (iii) number of members of the organization; (iv) number of employees at the location and summary of their responsibilities (USCIS may request employee list); (v) number of aliens holding religious-worker status currently or within past five years; (vi) number of religious-worker petitions/applications filed in past five years; (vii) title and detailed daily duties of the offered position; (viii) whether compensation is salaried or non-salaried and details; (ix) that employment is at least 20 hours/week; (x) specific employment location(s); and (xi) that the alien will not be engaged in secular employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial evidence for petitioning organization (tax-exempt status)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petition must include initial evidence relating to the petitioning organization’s tax-exempt status and religious nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence: (i) valid IRS determination letter showing tax-exempt status; or (ii) for group tax-exempt organizations, a valid IRS letter establishing the group's tax-exempt status; or (iii) for bona fide affiliated organizations granted tax-exempt status as something other than a religious organization under 501(c)(3): (A) valid IRS determination letter; (B) organizing instrument specifying religious purpose; (C) organizational literature describing religious activities; (D) a signed religious denomination certification of affiliation submitted with the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of qualifications for a minister
rubrics_metrics.description: If the alien is a minister, the petitioner must submit proof of ministerial qualifications and acceptance by the denomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence includes: (i) a copy of the alien's certificate of ordination or similar documents; and (ii) documents showing acceptance of qualifications and evidence of completion of prescribed theological education at an accredited theological institution (transcripts, curriculum, accreditation evidence), OR (iii) for denominations without prescribed theological education, evidence of the denomination's ordination requirements, duties allowed by ordination, levels of ordination, and the alien's completion of those requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence relating to compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial evidence must state how the petitioner intends to compensate the alien or whether the alien will be self-supporting and provide verifiable documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation may be salaried or non-salaried. Evidence may include past compensation for similar positions; budgets; verifiable documentation that room and board will be provided; IRS documents (W-2, certified tax returns) if available. If IRS documentation is unavailable, explain absence and provide comparable verifiable documentation. For self-supporting aliens, petitioner must submit documentation showing the position is part of an established program for temporary, uncompensated missionary work and evidence of the program's features and the alien's acceptance; also submit bank records, budgets, or other verifiable evidence of sources of self-support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and evidentiary requirements for an established program for temporary, uncompensated missionary work
rubrics_metrics.description: An established program for temporary, uncompensated work is a missionary program with specific characteristics permitting self-supporting R-1 classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program characteristics: (1) foreign workers have previously participated in R-1 status; (2) missionary workers are traditionally uncompensated; (3) organization provides formal missionary training; (4) participation is an established element of religious development in the denomination. Evidence required: proof the organization has such a program, denomination maintains missionary programs in U.S. and abroad, the worker's acceptance into program, description of religious duties, and verifiable financial evidence of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of previous R-1 employment for extension requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of R-1 status must include initial evidence documenting prior R-1 employment and compensation/support during that employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If salaried, submit IRS documentation (W-2, certified tax returns) reflecting work and compensation for preceding two years. If non-salaried, submit IRS documentation if available, or explanation and verifiable evidence of financial support (stipends, room/board) such as description of living location, lease, or other acceptable evidence. If no salary and self-supported, submit audited financial statements, bank records, brokerage statements, trust documents, or other verifiable evidence of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change or addition of employers for R-1 aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-1 alien may not be compensated by any religious organization other than the one for which a petition has been approved, unless prior approval obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A different or additional employer must file a separate petition with the required supplement, supporting documents, and fee as prescribed in 8 CFR 106.2 to obtain prior approval of such employment. Failure to obtain approval may render the alien out of status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer notification obligations when R-1 employment changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved employer must notify DHS if the R-1 alien is working less than required hours, is released, or otherwise terminates employment before the authorized period expires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification must occur within 14 days using procedures set forth in petition instructions or otherwise prescribed by USCIS on its website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonimmigrant intent requirement for R-1/R-2 aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-1/R-2 classified alien shall maintain an intention to depart the United States upon expiration or termination of status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a nonimmigrant petition, application for admission, change of status, or extension in R classification may not be denied solely because of a filed or approved request for permanent labor certification or an immigrant visa preference petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS inspections, evaluations, verifications, and compliance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may verify supporting evidence by any means it deems appropriate, including on-site inspections of the petitioning organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspections may include facility tours, interviews with officials, review of selected records related to immigration law compliance, interviews with other individuals, and review of other pertinent records. Inspections may cover headquarters, satellite locations, or planned work locations. Pre-approval inspections may be a condition for approval; satisfactory completion is required if conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial notification and appeal rights for R-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will provide written notification of reasons for denial; the petitioner may appeal under 8 CFR 103.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification follows the requirements of 8 CFR 103.3(a)(1). Appeals must be filed in accordance with 8 CFR 103.3 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of approved R-1 petitions — director discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: The director may revoke a petition at any time, even after expiration of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation is an exercise of the director's discretion and can occur when new information or concerns arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic revocation of approved R-1 petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Approval of any petition is automatically revoked if the petitioner ceases to exist or files a written withdrawal of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automatic revocations are not subject to appeal under the revocation appeal rules for notices on revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation on notice — grounds and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The director shall send a notice of intent to revoke if certain grounds are found, with opportunity for rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds include: (1) beneficiary no longer employed in the capacity specified; (2) statement of facts in petition were not true and correct; (3) petitioner violated terms/conditions of approved petition; (4) petitioner violated requirements of section 101(a)(15)(R) or paragraph (r) of this section; or (5) approval violated paragraph (r) or involved gross error. Notice must include detailed grounds and time allowed (30 days) for petitioner's rebuttal; director will consider relevant evidence presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal of a revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition revoked on notice in whole or in part may be appealed under 8 CFR 103.3; automatic revocations may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow appeal procedures in 8 CFR 103.3 for revocation-on-notice cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of NATO nonimmigrant classifications (NATO-1 to NATO-7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific nonimmigrant classifications assigned to NATO officials, employees, members of forces, civilian components, attendants, servants, and their families according to role and relationship to NATO entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NATO-1 through NATO-6 define principals, representatives, staff, officials, experts, and civilian employees; NATO-7 covers attendants/servants/personal employees authorized to work only for the NATO principal from whom they derive status. The page lists detailed role examples for each classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission and extension rules for NATO classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Admission, inspection exemptions, duration of admission, and extension increments differ by NATO class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NATO-1 through NATO-5 are normally exempt from inspection under 8 CFR 235.1(c). NATO-6 may be authorized admission for duration of status. NATO-7 may be admitted for not more than 3 years and may be granted extensions of temporary stay in increments of not more than 2 years. Extension for NATO-7 must include an employing official's statement describing continued employment, duties, and acknowledging sole employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of dependent for NATO principal aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: For employment purposes, dependents habitually residing in the same household include spouse, unmarried children under specified ages, and disabled unmarried children unable to care for themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categories: spouse; unmarried children under 21; unmarried sons/daughters under 23 in full-time post-secondary attendance; under 25 in full-time attendance if a formal bilateral employment agreement signed before Nov 21, 1988 and agreement does not specify age 23; unmarried sons/daughters with physical/mental disability (Service may require medical certification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent employment via formal bilateral employment agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependents may accept or continue unrestricted employment based on formal bilateral employment agreements upon favorable SACLANT recommendation and issuance of employment authorization by the Service under 8 CFR part 274a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department of State's Family Liaison Office (FLO) maintains the list of NATO Member States with such formal bilateral agreements. Application procedures are set forth in paragraph (s)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent employment via informal de facto reciprocal arrangements and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependents may be authorized employment based on OSD/FMRA certification of reciprocity and State FLO listing, subject to SACLANT recommendation and Service issuance of employment authorization, if specific conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions to be met: (A) both principal and dependent maintain appropriate NATO status; (B) principal's U.S. assignment expected to last more than 6 months; (C) reciprocity not prohibited by the NATO Member State; (D) proposed employment not in occupations listed in Dept. of Labor Schedule B or otherwise deemed oversupplied (part-time student exceptions); (E) employment not contrary to U.S. interests (e.g., criminal records, immigration violations, illegal work history, or inability to show tax/Social Security payments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of formal bilateral agreements and de facto arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability is based on the NATO Member State employing the principal alien and, for de facto arrangements, the principal must be a national of that state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependents of SACLANT employees receive appropriate privileges based on the nationality of the SACLANT employee and listings maintained by State's FLO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedures for dependent employment under bilateral/de facto arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependents must submit a complete application for employment authorization (Forms I-765 and I-566) properly completed and submitted to SACLANT for certification and forwarding to the Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include: (i) Form I-566 certified by SACLANT for forwarding; (ii) where numerical limitations exist, certifying officer must confirm limits not reached; (iii) SACLANT keeps copies for 3 years; (iv) de facto arrangement applicants must attach a prospective employer statement describing position, duties, hours, salary, and verifying qualifications; (v) students must submit certified statements from educational institutions; (vi) disabled dependents must submit medical certification describing condition; (vii) Service may require additional supporting documentation after consultation with SACLANT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized period for dependent employment under NATO rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If approved, dependent employment authorization is granted in increments not exceeding 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow approval period and extension practices as specified by the Service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income tax and Social Security liability for employed dependents
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependents granted employment authorization are responsible for payment of all federal, state, and local income taxes, employment-related taxes, and Social Security contributions on remuneration received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dependents must comply with all tax and Social Security obligations arising from employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: No appeal from denial of dependent employment permission
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no administrative appeal from a denial of permission to accept or continue employment under the NATO-dependent employment paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials are final under this paragraph; other administrative avenues are not provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized employment consequences for NATO-classified aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: A NATO-classified alien (other than principal aliens) who engages in employment outside the scope of this paragraph may be considered in violation of status pursuant to section 237(a)(1)(C)(i) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A NATO principal alien engaging in employment outside official position may also be considered in violation of status under the same statutory provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-5 nonimmigrant classification criteria (alien witness/informant in criminal matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien may be classified as an S-5 if, pursuant to a Form I-854 application by an interested federal or state law enforcement authority (LEA) and Commissioner discretion, the alien: (i) possesses critical reliable information concerning a criminal organization or enterprise; (ii) is willing to supply or has supplied such information to federal/state LEA; and (iii) is essential to the success of an authorized criminal investigation or prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification requires submission by an LEA on Form I-854 and discretionary determination by the Commissioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-6 nonimmigrant classification criteria (counterterrorism witness/informant)
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien may be classified as an S-6 if, as determined jointly by Secretary of State and Commissioner on Form I-854 application by an eligible federal LEA: (i) possesses critical reliable information concerning a terrorist organization, enterprise, or operation; (ii) is willing to supply or has supplied such information to a federal LEA; (iii) is in danger or has been placed in danger as a result; and (iv) is eligible to receive a reward under 22 U.S.C. 2708(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S-6 requires joint Secretary/Commissioner determination and LEA certification of eligibility for S-6 classification; numerical limits apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derivative S-7 classification for family members of S aliens
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien spouse, married/unmarried son/daughter, or parent of an S-5 or S-6 alien may be granted derivative S classification (S-7) when accompanying or following to join, at the discretion of the Commissioner or Secretary/Commissioner jointly, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivative beneficiaries must be identified by the requesting LEA on Form I-854; family members not identified on the Form I-854 will not be eligible for S classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file requests for S nonimmigrant classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a federal or state law enforcement authority (LEA) directly in need of the information may file an application on Form I-854 requesting S classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The LEA must complete Form I-854 with necessary endorsements and attachments and agree that no promises have been or will be made guaranteeing continued presence, adjustment, or other means of remaining beyond statutorily authorized terms. The alien and any derivative 18+ must sign a statement acknowledging the restrictions of S classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: District director, U.S. Attorney, and LEA certification roles in S filings
rubrics_metrics.description: District directors must advise requestors; U.S. Attorneys must certify and endorse applications; LEA certifications must be at appropriate governmental levels and include detailed attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District director referral: refer eligible LEAs to the Commissioner. U.S. Attorney certification: must certify and endorse and agree no promises re status will be made. LEA certification: must be at seat-of-government level (if federal) or highest state LEA level, and provide attachments establishing nature of cooperation, need for presence, excludability conduct/conditions, and factors warranting discretionary waiver by the Attorney General; attachments may include affidavits, statements, memoranda, or similar documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing procedure for S nonimmigrant requests to Assistant Attorney General
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon completion, the LEA forwards Form I-854 with attachments to the Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division, who forwards properly certified applications within numerical limits to the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Assistant Attorney General will forward only properly certified applications that fall within the annual numerical limitation. The Assistant Attorney General also ensures all information related to application basis, need, and excludability is provided to the Service before action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Attorney General review, advisory panel, and certification contents for S requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division, reviews complete applications and may convene an advisory panel; certifications to the Commissioner must include specific items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review: ensure all information and grounds of excludability are provided and consider negative and favorable factors. Advisory panel (if necessary) may include Service, Marshals Service, FBI, DEA, Criminal Division, State Dept., and other LEAs to prioritize cases under numerical limits. Certification must contain: (1) information/attachments relating to excludability under section 212(a); (2) each law section under which alien appears inadmissible; (3) reasons waivers of inadmissibility are justifiable and in the national interest; (4) detailed statement on eligibility, cooperation, and government need; (5) intended date of arrival; (6) length of proposed stay; (7) purpose of stay; (8) statement that application falls within the numerical limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Commissioner and numerical limitation rules for S requests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assistant Attorney General forwards only certified, qualified applications that fall within the annual numerical limitation to the Commissioner; S-6 requires Secretary of State certification of eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistant Attorney General forwards S-5 certified applications and forwards S-6 certified applications that are certified by Secretary of State for eligibility, all subject to numerical caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making and waiver delegation for S nonimmigrant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Attorney General’s authority to waive inadmissibility under section 212 is delegated to the Commissioner for S classifications and is exercised only upon certification by the Assistant Attorney General, Criminal Division; this certification is nonreviewable regarding its law enforcement significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner makes final approval/denial. Upon approval, admission authorized for up to 3 years. Upon denial, Assistant Attorney General and relevant LEA are notified; Assistant Attorney General may concur or object (7-day response period), with referral to Deputy AG if objection; alien/LEA have no appeal right from denials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Secretary of State for S visa processing
rubrics_metrics.description: No request for S nonimmigrant visa classification may be presented to the Secretary of State unless it is approved and forwarded by the Commissioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only Commissioner-forwarded, approved requests reach State Department for visa processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions of S status
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien witness or informant is responsible for certifying and fulfilling the terms and conditions specified on Form I-854 as a condition of status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The alien must comply with all certifications and conditions in Form I-854; failure to do so may affect status.
